title: ADA Channel Column Specification Registry
description: Registry of reusable schema:PropertyValueSpecification channel column definitions derived from technique TAPP workbooks. Each $def constrains one column of the channel table, a channel being an instrument selection position -- a mass, a Faraday cup, an energy-loss edge, an X-ray line -- as distinct from the analyte measured on it. TAPP building blocks reference these definitions via fragment $refs so they resolve locally through the building-block register. The root only hosts $defs; it has no instantiable properties of its own.

empa_backgroundCountingTime.title: Background Counting Time
empa_backgroundCountingTime.description: Total time spent counting at off-peak background position(s) in seconds, summed across all background positions.

empa_backgroundPosition.title: Background Position(s)
empa_backgroundPosition.description: Location(s) of off-peak background measurement(s) relative to the peak, in mm or sin-theta, and whether on the high- or low-energy side.

empa_dwellTimePerPixel.title: Dwell Time per Pixel
empa_dwellTimePerPixel.description: Time spent acquiring X-ray signal at each pixel during X-ray mapping, in milliseconds. For WDS: one value per spectrometer assignment per pixel. For EDS: total live-time per spectrum per pixel, a single value.

empa_peakCountingTime.title: Peak Counting Time
empa_peakCountingTime.description: Time spent counting X-ray intensity at the peak position, in seconds. Adjustments stay within procedure-defined bounds.

empa_sequence.title: Sequence
empa_sequence.description: Order in which spectrometer assignments are acquired, and — where the element suite exceeds the number of spectrometers — the passes the acquisition is divided into. Within a single pass all assigned spectrometers collect simultaneously, including at every pixel in X-ray mapping; a suite larger than the spectrometer count therefore requires the acquisition to be run more than once, each pass covering a different subset of elements.

empa_wdsPhaSetting.title: WDS PHA Setting
empa_wdsPhaSetting.description: Pulse height analyzer (PHA) setting for the WDS detector. Integral mode accepts all pulses above a threshold; Differential mode selects a narrow energy window to reject higher-order reflections and escape peaks.

laMcicpms_faradayCupAmplifierResistorVal.title: Faraday Cup Amplifier Resistor Values
laMcicpms_faradayCupAmplifierResistorVal.description: Resistance values (Ω) of the feedback resistors in the Faraday cup amplifiers. Standard amplifiers use 10¹¹ Ω resistors, yielding 1 V per ~6.24 × 10⁶ ion counts per second. Report the resistor value per cup position, or note 'all 10¹¹ Ω' if uniform.

laMcicpms_faradayCupGainCalibrationMetho.title: Faraday Cup Gain Calibration Method
laMcicpms_faradayCupGainCalibrationMetho.description: Method used to calibrate the relative gain (amplification factor) of each Faraday cup amplifier at the start of or during each analytical session. Common approaches: instrument internal gain calibration routine (measures signal in each cup sequentially using a common beam), amplifier rotation procedure, or measurement of a known isotope ratio solution in each cup. For instruments with SEM detectors, also describes the SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration sequence. Specify frequency (per session, per block, weekly).

laMcicpms_integrationTimePerCycle.title: Integration Time per Cycle
laMcicpms_integrationTimePerCycle.description: Duration of signal integration per measurement cycle (seconds).

laMcicpms_interferenceCorrectionMethod.title: Interference Correction Method
laMcicpms_interferenceCorrectionMethod.description: Equation or procedure used to calculate and remove each interference contribution, together with how its magnitude was established - a monitor mass measured simultaneously and scaled by natural abundance ratios, a production-rate factor measured on a reference material or interference standard solution, or a tailing factor measured on a pure standard. Name the reference material used.

laMcicpms_interferingSpecies.title: Interfering Species
laMcicpms_interferingSpecies.description: The isobaric, polyatomic and doubly charged species that overlap the measured masses and are corrected in data reduction - direct isobars, oxides and argides, hydrides, and abundance-sensitivity tailing from an adjacent large beam. Name each species and the mass it affects.

laMcicpms_ionCounterDeadTime.title: Ion Counter Dead Time
laMcicpms_ionCounterDeadTime.description: Dead time of the ion-counting detector(s), used in the dead-time correction applied to high count rates. Distinct from pulse/analog cross-calibration, which relates the two detector modes rather than correcting counting losses within the pulse-counting mode.

laMcicpms_massResolutionAssignment.title: Mass Resolution Assignment
laMcicpms_massResolutionAssignment.description: Mass resolution mode used for acquisition. One target species may be acquired at more than one resolution, so the assignment is per acquired mass rather than per element. The overall mode(s) used in the procedure are recorded in Mass Resolution Setting (Group 3).

solutionMcicpms_interferingSpecies.description: The isobaric, polyatomic and doubly charged species that overlap the measured masses and are corrected in data reduction - direct isobars, oxides and argides, hydrides, and abundance-sensitivity tailing from an adjacent large beam. Name each species and the mass it affects.

solutionMcicpms_isobaricInterferenceCorr.title: Isobaric Interference Corrections Applied
solutionMcicpms_isobaricInterferenceCorr.description: Whether mathematical corrections for residual isobaric or polyatomic interferences are applied in data reduction, supplementary to any interference suppression achieved by chemical separation or mass resolution. In solution MC-ICP-MS, chemical separation is the primary interference mitigation; mathematical corrections address residual contributions. Common examples: 204Hg on 204Pb; abundance sensitivity tailing of 238U onto 236U and 235U.

solutionMcicpms_massResolutionAssignment.description: Mass resolution mode used for acquisition. One target species may be acquired at more than one resolution, so the assignment is per acquired mass rather than per element. The overall mode(s) used in the procedure are recorded in Mass Resolution Setting (Group 3).

solutionMcicpms_spectralInterferenceCorr.title: Spectral Interference Corrections Applied
solutionMcicpms_spectralInterferenceCorr.description: Whether mathematical corrections for isobaric, polyatomic or residual interferences are applied in data reduction, supplementary to any suppression already achieved by chemical separation, mass resolution, or a collision/reaction cell. Detail for each affected mass is carried by Interfering Species and Interference Correction Method.

solutionQicpms_dwellTimePerMass.title: Dwell Time per Mass
solutionQicpms_dwellTimePerMass.description: Count (dwell) time at the mass position, in milliseconds. Where the procedure defines it per sweep or per scan rather than per measurement, state that basis.

solutionQicpms_spectralInterferenceCorre.title: Spectral Interference Corrections Applied

tem_eelsBackgroundSubtractionMethod.title: EELS Background Subtraction Method
tem_eelsBackgroundSubtractionMethod.description: Method used to subtract the background beneath the ionization edge of interest to extract the net edge signal. Record 'N/A' where EELS is not listed in Spectroscopic Detector(s).

tem_eelsDetectionLimit.title: EELS Detection Limit
tem_eelsDetectionLimit.description: Estimated detection limit or minimum detectable concentration for target edges under this procedure. Record 'N/A' where EELS is not listed in Spectroscopic Detector(s).

tem_eelsSensitivityAndDetectionLimit.title: EELS Sensitivity and Detection Limit
tem_eelsSensitivityAndDetectionLimit.description: Practical energy resolution (ZLP FWHM measured at operating conditions) and estimated detection limit or minimum detectable concentration for target edges under this procedure. Record 'N/A' where EELS is not listed in Spectroscopic Detector(s).
